CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to evaluate treatment modifications for generalized anxiety disorder, insomnia, persistent fatigue, and tension-type headaches. Focus on assessing symptom management, medication adherence, and overall quality of life since the last appointment.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up visit, reporting mixed results from the recent adjustments to his treatment plan. He states that while his anxiety levels have shown slight improvement, he still experiences episodes of irritability, particularly in high-stress work situations. He has been consistent with his sertraline regimen of 300 mg daily, but he continues to struggle with cognitive issues, specifically concentration and memory, which he describes as cloudy and frustrating during his daily tasks.
The frequency of his tension-type headaches remains unchanged, occurring approximately twice weekly with an intensity of 4 to 6 out of 10. Mr. Smith reports that topiramate at 150 mg daily continues to provide some relief; however, he has increased his ibuprofen usage to four times a month due to the persistent headaches. He expresses concern that the headaches may be exacerbated by his ongoing work stress and fatigue.
Sleep patterns have remained stable, averaging 7 to 8 hours per night, supported by trazodone and melatonin. However, he continues to experience significant morning grogginess, which he describes as a barrier to initiating his daily activities. Mr. Smith has been proactive in managing his fatigue, reporting that he has started incorporating short walks during his breaks at work, which he feels has contributed positively to his energy levels.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 300 mg daily (continued) 2. Trazodone 75 mg at bedtime (continued) 3. Lisinopril 10 mg daily (continued) 4. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief (increased frequency) 5. Amitriptyline 50 mg nightly (continued) 6. Topiramate 150 mg daily (continued) 7. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (continued) 8. Melatonin 3 mg at bedtime (continued) 9. Modafinil 100 mg in the morning (initiated to address persistent fatigue)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith maintains a commitment to regular physical activity, including brisk walking and hiking on weekends. He continues to monitor his caffeine intake and adheres to a balanced diet, which he believes aids in managing his anxiety. His mindfulness practices, including meditation and yoga, remain essential components of his routine. However, he acknowledges that work-related stress has occasionally impeded his ability to consistently engage in these activities.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Anxiety levels slightly improved; persistent irritability noted; sleep quality satisfactory; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms. - Neurological: Stable headache frequency; no dizziness or visual disturbances reported. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Improved fatigue management reported, particularly with the introduction of modafinil, with no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 118/76 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert, oriented; appears mildly fatigued but engaged; mood appears anxious with moderate distress. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed; no tenderness in the temporal region. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears anxious with moderate distress.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 300 mg daily. Recommend ongoing cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) to further address irritability and cognitive concerns. Monitor response to the current regimen and consider potential dose adjustments if symptoms do not improve. 2. Insomnia: Continue trazodone at 75 mg at bedtime and melatonin 3 mg nightly; reassess in one month for efficacy and any side effects. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue topiramate at 150 mg daily; maintain headache diary to monitor frequency and intensity. Consider referral to a neurologist if there is no improvement or if new symptoms develop. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Continue modafinil at 100 mg in the morning; monitor for efficacy in alleviating fatigue. Reinforce the importance of stress management techniques and lifestyle modifications, including regular physical activity and adequate hydration.
Follow-up appointment is scheduled for 2029-07-25 to evaluate symptom progression, medication efficacy, and discuss any new concerns. Mr. Smith is encouraged to maintain open communication regarding his treatment response and any lifestyle changes he implements.
